items.titel: Economic Trade and Atmospheric Transport in Shaping China’s Nitrogen Deposition Patterns
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition in China is driven not only by local emissions but also by global economic demand and transboundary atmospheric transport. Unraveling these dual influences is critical for effective environmental governance. Here, we integrate an economic-emission analysis with a high-resolution atmospheric chemical transport model to quantify, for the first time, the distinct roles of domestic consumption, international trade, and atmospheric transport in shaping China’s nitrogen deposition patterns. We find that domestic consumption is the dominant contributor, responsible for 67.6% of the total deposition, involving a substantial interprovincial transfer of emissions from affluent coastal provinces to less developed inland regions. International trade attributes 7.8% of China’s deposition to foreign consumption, primarily driven by demand from the USA and Western Europe. In contrast, trans-national atmospheric transport directly accounts for 12.8%, with a disproportionately high impact on ecologically sensitive western China. Natural sources contribute the remaining 11.8%. Our results reveal a complex web of drivers extending beyond China’s borders. Mitigating nitrogen deposition, therefore, requires moving beyond local emission controls to embrace consumption-based accountability and enhanced international cooperation on both trade and atmospheric pollution to protect vulnerable ecosystems.

items.titel: Exploring the value of thematic urban ecosystem accounts in Western Balkan countries to inform urban greening actions
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban ecological health is increasingly prioritised in Europe, as reflected in the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030, the Nature Restoration Regulation, and the amended Regulation on Environmental-Economic Accounts. Translating these commitments into effective greening policy and planning actions that halt and reverse urban ecological degradation requires standardised, spatially explicit indicators. This study explores the utility of the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting–Ecosystem Accounting (SEEA-EA) framework for developing thematic urban ecosystem accounts as integrated metrics to inform urban greening in the Western Balkans. We constructed pilot accounts for the Western Balkans for 2018, with particular focus on Horizon-funded CROSS-REIS countries, where local accounts were also developed for representative municipalities (Kranj, Rijeka, Niš, Podgorica, Tirana) for 2018 and 2021. Accounts include ecosystem extent, four condition indicators (imperviousness, green space, tree cover, PM 10 concentration), and the ecosystem service air filtration, estimated via PM 10 deposition onto vegetation. Results were benchmarked nationally against EU-EFTA countries and the UK and locally against pilot Italian municipalities of the National Biodiversity Future Center. Western Balkan urban ecosystems fall within the European range but display a more homogeneous profile, confirmed by permutation tests and largely explained by shared climate and urban classes. items.titel: Ambition without alignment: Pollinators in the EU Nature Restoration Law
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Pollinators are essential for life on Earth. They enable the reproduction of most flowering plants and support biodiversity as well as food systems. However, their numbers are in great decline. Research finds a continuing decrease in pollinating insects each year. This article reviews whether EU Law is fit to address this challenge. First, this paper analyses the norms in the EU Nature Restoration Law (NRL) and the Delegated Regulation, finding that the NRL demands wide‐scale system change to comply with the targets set out. Second, it reviews what legal instruments and policies hold back these promises. Examples are the EU Pesticide Laws, EU climate laws, EU norms on light pollution, rules on Invasive Alien Species and, most pressingly, the proposed EU Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) budget. In the end, this paper concludes that the EU also has a responsibility to support the implementation of the NRL beyond interpretation manuals and soft guidance. It must fund, streamline and revise its own architecture, strengthening many existing EU laws to ensure coherence.

items.titel: Microclimate Control for Outdoor Thermal Comfort in Apartment Residential Green Spaces: A Systematic Review of Climate-Responsive Design Strategies and Assessment Methods
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban overheating is an increasingly prevalent threat to the liveability and thermal comfort of outdoor spaces in residential apartment areas. While urban green spaces can regulate microclimates and mitigate heat, there remains a lack of evidence on how design interventions can integrate environmental performance with human comfort. Following PRISMA guidelines, this systematic review synthesises 22 peer-reviewed studies from Web of Science and Scopus (2015–2025), selected from an initial set of 187 records. The review reveals that existing studies primarily quantify environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity and wind speed while inadequately addressing multifactor interactions and subjective comfort responses. To address this gap, the review proposes an integrated framework that links environmental metrics, human perceptual data, and climate-responsive design strategies. The findings further reveal that vegetation configuration, shading, surface materials, and spatial layout are key design levers, although their effectiveness varies across climate zones. Notably, this review offers a novel contribution by systematically identifying the interplay between objective microclimatic variables and subjective human comfort responses—an interaction largely overlooked in prior apartment-green-space research. items.titel: ADVANCING ESG THROUGH GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE SOLUTIONS IN RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED MALAWIAN CITIES: AN EXPLORATORY QUALITATIVE STUDY
items.samenvatting_bron: Malawi’s urban areas are increasingly vulnerable to climate-related disasters, including flooding, landslides, and extreme winds, while conventional infrastructure struggles under these pressures dueto outdated designs, limited maintenance, and poor climate adaptation. This study aims to examine how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG)-aligned green infrastructure (GI) can strengthen urban resilience in resource-constrained Malawian cities, with a focus on Blantyre and Zomba. A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using systematic document analysis of secondary sources, with thematic analysis applied to identify patterns in climate risk, governance constraints, and lessons for context-appropriate green infrastructure strategies. Findings show that GI interventions, including urban wetlands, permeable pavements, slope vegetation, and tree planting, offer significant environmental, social, and governance benefits: they reduce flood and landslide risks, improve waterquality, support biodiversity, create green jobs, enhance public health, and foster community inclusion, while strong governance ensures sustainability through institutional accountability, integrated planning, and transparent financing. A key limitation of this study is the absence of primary stakeholder interviews, which limits direct insights into municipal implementation challenges. items.titel: The population and the habitats of Common Swift Apus apus in the Brussels Capital Region
items.samenvatting_bron: This article presents the results of a survey of the Brussels population of Common Swift which was carried out between 2016 and 2018 under the programme "Monitoring of the State of the Brussels Environment" (for which Aves-Natagora has been collaborating with Bruxelles Environnement since 1992). The main objective was to improve our knowledge of the aspects of the habitat that are preferred by this population so as to improve our understanding of how the population may be preserved and its decline halted. Also a standardised protocol was developed for routine monitoring at regional level.The results have enabled the definition of the best sites for such monitoring. The densities obtained in this work are consistent with figures in the literature, suggesting that the methodology is adequate and that the figures obtained here can provide a useful basis of comparison for the future. Most of the colonies that we found were small. As regards habitat, we found that most nests were located under the cornices in non-residential areas (with mostly semi-detached buildings), located along narrow roads.

items.titel: eDNA metabarcoding reveals invertebrate diversity in the blackwater pools of southeast Queensland peatlands
items.samenvatting_bron: Despite harbouring a disproportionate diversity of rare and endemic species, the pyrophilic peatlands of southeast Queensland remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding their invertebrate communities. In the physically and chemically extreme blackwater pools, meiofaunal assemblages likely form critical trophic links but have never been described due to their small size and low public profile. This study used 18S environmental DNA metabarcoding to characterize invertebrate communities across three peatland sites. We detected 48 unique taxa across 10 phyla, including five invertebrate phyla previously unrecorded in these ecosystems (Cnidaria, Rotifera, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda and Gastrotricha). Metabarcoding exceeded the resolution achieved by field surveys for morphologically cryptic microcrustaceans; however, field surveys achieved better resolution for larger hexapods, demonstrating that the methods target distinct components of the invertebrate community. Key life-history traits were shared across the detected meiofaunal communities, including rapid maturation, parthenogenetic reproduction, and dormancy capabilities. These traits likely enable rapid community recovery and ecosystem stabilization following fire disturbances characteristic of pyrophilic peatlands. Collectively, these taxa occupy a crucial and previously undocumented intermediary trophic link between microbial production and higher consumers. items.titel: Strategic implementation of green roofs for urban pluvial flood risk reduction: A case study of Milan, Italy
items.samenvatting_bron: The rise in intensity and frequency of extreme precipitation events is increasing the concern regarding pluvial floods in European cities. Urbanisation exacerbates the impacts of pluvial floods by affecting the infiltration process. Nature-based solutions, particularly Green Roofs (GRs), are promoted to mitigate these risks, as GRs can be implemented on existing buildings without requiring additional ground space. This study presents a risk-based framework to evaluate the potential of GRs in reducing pluvial flood risk in Milan by examining three implementation strategies, namely Water Depth (WD), Area (Ar), and Random Iteration (ITE). The framework integrates a hybrid hazard model, combining the empirical Curve Number method with a Cellular Automata approach using a hydrograph. The proposed hybrid approach enables us to link land-use-driven changes in flood volume to flood propagation. Extreme rainfall events with durations of 1, 6, and 24 hours were derived from ERA5. Residential building exposure data were extracted from OpenStreetMap and municipal datasets. Vulnerability was integrated within the framework using the INSYDE model, complemented by four additional vulnerability functions for sensitivity analysis. Results indicate that GRs can effectively reduce pluvial flood-induced losses, with reductions of 16-69% across different rainfall durations. items.titel: Review article: Mountain flash floods: from hazard formation to disaster risk reduction pathways
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Flash floods in mountainous regions are becoming more frequent and destructive under climate warming, yet cross-regional understanding of their triggering mechanisms, cascading impacts, and governance remains fragmented. This review synthesises 1,967 studies published during 2000–2025 to establish a globally comparable baseline of mountain flash-flood research. By integrating bibliometric and topic analyses with qualitative synthesis, we reveal pronounced geographical and thematic imbalances, with research concentrated in Europe and Asia. At the same time, many high-risk mountain regions in Africa and South America remain overlooked. Across regions, flash-flood initiation and impacts are shown to be strongly state-dependent and coupled, emerging from interactions between storm intensity, duration and spatial concentration, antecedent hydrological conditions, and hillslope-channel connectivity. This coupling helps explain why fixed rainfall thresholds are difficult to generalise and highlights the need for dynamic, multi-source early-warning approaches. Comparing evidence on early warning, structural protection, and Nature-Based Solutions, the review shows that cascading processes dominate risk management challenges. We therefore propose an adaptive governance framework that links monitoring and forecasting, spatial planning, grey-green integration, and basin-scale risk sharing under non-stationary climate conditions. items.titel: AI-Based Decision-Making Framework for Climate Change-Induced Flood Risk Management and Urban Resilience
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change has intensified the frequency and severity of urban flooding, creating unprecedented challenges for municipalities worldwide. This study develops an AI-based decision-making framework that integrates machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and geospatial analytics to enhance urban flood risk management and resilience planning. The framework employs ensemble machine learning algorithms including Random Forest, XG Boost, and Cat Boost for flood susceptibility mapping, coupled with SHAP-based interpretability to decode model predictions and translate them into actionable policy insights at administrative scales. A city-scale digital twin component enables real-time flood impact simulation and cascading infrastructure disruption analysis, while a multi-criteria decision support module prioritizes adaptation investments based on economic risk assessment and equity considerations. The framework was validated using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 SAR data and hydrological records across diverse urban environments, demonstrating superior predictive performance with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values exceeding 0.95 for ensemble models. Results reveal that elevation, proximity to hydrological features, and impervious surface density consistently emerge as dominant flood drivers, with their relative importance varying significantly across districts. items.titel: Beyond Average Runoff Reduction: Event-Based Assessment of Climate Adaptation Benefits and Flood Vulnerability of Blue–Green Roofs
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change increases the need for urban stormwater management systems that can maintain hydrological performance under severe rainfall conditions. Although green and blue–green roofs are widely used as nature-based solutions for runoff management, their performance is commonly evaluated using average or cumulative runoff reduction, which may not capture differences that emerge during severe events. This study applied an event-based assessment to 31 rainfall events monitored on a conventional roof (Control), a Blue–Green Roof (BGR), and a Smart Blue–Green Roof (Smart BGR). Climate Adaptation Benefit (CAB) was calculated by integrating relative runoff reduction with rainfall severity, while the additional benefit of Smart BGR was evaluated using the difference in CAB (ΔCAB). The Severity-Weighted Runoff Vulnerability Index (FVI) and Severity-Weighted Runoff Vulnerability Reduction (FVR) were used to assess runoff-related vulnerability across four rainfall severity classes. Both systems provided substantial benefits under low rainfall severity, with relatively small differences. However, Smart BGR generally showed higher CAB and positive ΔCAB than BGR, while maintaining lower FVI and greater FVR under the observed higher-severity rainfall conditions. These findings suggest that the primary value of Smart BGR lies in maintaining greater climate adaptation benefits under severe rainfall conditions. items.titel: A harmonization-based framework for cross-sensor super-resolution of Sentinel-2 imagery for coastal applications
items.samenvatting_bron: High-resolution (HR) satellite imagery is essential for coastal mapping, ocean analysis, and long-term environmental monitoring; however, acquiring it is constrained by hardware limitations and high costs. Freely available low-resolution (LR) archives, such as those from Sentinel-2 (S2), offer global coverage and frequent revisits, but their 10 m native resolution is insufficient for fine-scale analysis. This study presents HARBOR (Harmonization-based Adaptive Resolution Boosting for Optical Remote sensing), an integrated harmonization-based workflow that combines established radiometric harmonization and sub-pixel convolutional super-resolution (SR) components and adapts them to four-band coastal S2–PlanetScope (PS) data. Rather than proposing a new network architecture, HARBOR addresses a gap in the way satellite SR is commonly assembled, where network optimization receives most of the attention and cross-sensor radiometric inconsistency is treated as a preprocessing detail.
